body:
Also noticed that other rules have similar results when comments are involved (e.g., no-spaced-func: 2):

```
describe/*.only*/('foo', function () {});
```

```
error  Unexpected space between function name and paren  no-spaced-func
```

`padded-blocks` shouldn’t count comments as empty lines, there is a [test-case for this scenario](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/89b1ee3a06370197e060fe6688b40d1b587ee1af/tests/lib/rules/padded-blocks.js#L37).

Can you provide more information? Do you use the default parser `espree` or a different parser?
Disabling the babel-eslint parser makes the `padded-blocks` error go away, but `no-spaced-func` still produces errors.

Let's focus on the `no-spaced-func` issue. We're probably mistakenly treating comments as spaces because we're just checking the location of the two tokens (and the comment doesn't appear in the token list).
@nzakas I guess there are more rules affected by this bug, see https://github.com/eslint/eslint/search?utf8=%E2%9C%93&q=isSpaced.

issue.body:
I wanted to use the rule `no-warning-comments`, however the ast doesn't have the comment node when passed to ESLint.
Is there any plan to support comments?
I wanted to try it out myself, but I don't know well enough the ast structure to add node to it. I saw that all the comments are available on `ast.comments`, but are not used in `acornToEsprima`

body: Ack! Okay, we probably need to externalize that into a common utility so we can fix it once.
I'm wonder how much would break if we add comments into the token list. Might need to investigate that as a better long-term solution.

> I'm wonder how much would break if we add comments into the token list.

I've investigated doing something along these lines (inspired by what millermedeiros/rocambole does with tokens), but merging tokens and comments was a big enough perf hit (~30% iirc) that I didn't pursue it much further. I got far enough to know we'd probably need to augment the tokens API with methods that skipped comments, so that style rules would get comments and semantic rules wouldn't.

It seems like there should be a fairly inexpensive way to do this. I'm assuming you were doing some array splicing, but I'm not sure that's necessary. In token store, we're already iterating over each token to setup the lookups. What if we just, in that same loop, checked to see if a comment comes next and add `leadingComments` and `trailingComments` as we do for nodes?
